subject: Meteorology
title: Geostationary Weather Satellites
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Geostationary Weather Satellites.

hook.text: Geostationary satellites orbit at 35,786 km—matching Earth's rotation to watch the same view continuously.

buildup.text: This fixed vantage point lets them capture images every 1–10 minutes—essential for tracking fast-changing weather.

discovery.text: GOES satellites over the Western Hemisphere produce the animated cloud loops seen in every TV weather report.

twist.text: They can't see the poles well due to their equatorial orbit—polar-orbiting satellites fill that gap from much closer.

climax.text: A ring of geostationary satellites now watches nearly the entire globe in real time—no storm escapes their view.

punchline.text: Always watching, never moving—the eye that never blinks.

quiz.question: Why are geostationary satellites positioned over the equator?
options: They match Earth's rotation to maintain a fixed view
